catalog_quote: 11. The Quantity of the Syllable is important for the position of the accent and in versification. a. A syllable containing a long vowel or a diphthong is said to be long by nature: as, ma-ter, aes, au-la. b. A syllable containing a short vowel followed by two consonants (except a mute before 1 or.r) or by a double consonant (x, z) is said to be long by position, but the vowel is pronounced short: as, est, ter-ra, sax-um, Me-zen-tius. ... c. A syllable containing a short vowel followed by a mute before 1 or r is properly short, but may be used as long in verse. ... 12. Words of two syllables are accented on the first syllable: as, Ro'ma, fi'dés, tan'go. Words of more than two syllables are accented on the Penult if that is long (as, ami’cus, moné@'tur, contin'git); otherwise on the Antepenult (as, do/minus, a’licris, dissocia’bilis). a. audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding A&G 1903 secs. 11-12 passage is verbatim in the held archive.org scanned text (lines 1006-1025, 1077-1082, page headers 6 and 7) and in the held DCC digitization. (2) Deciding source is a 1903 school grammar, but the coding (weight-sensitive, right edge, penult if heavy else antepenult, disyllables initial, heavy = CVV+CVC) is independently confirmed by the held Hayes 1995 sec. 5.1.4 pp. 91-92 page pin, by Lehmann 2005 fetched sources now (mora formulation: accent on third-last mora with final syllable = 1 mora; any complex rhyme heavy), and by verbatim FTS snippets of Allen Vox Latina 1965/1978 ('penultimate if this is of heavy quantity... antepenultimate (regardless of quantity) if the penultimate is light'). No source opened contradicts the coding; Latin is the textbook case. (3) The 'contra' flag (11/24) is a tally artefact: the 13 misses are A&G's own declared exc

sources.quote: 'Latin here sides with the languages of the first group, in which any kind of complexity in the rhyme raises its weight to two moras' ... 'P12. Latin word accentuation 1. The weight of the last syllable is stipulated to be one mora. 2. Word accent falls on the third-last mora. 3. If the word is shorter, word accent falls on the first mora.'

sources.note: The standard dedicated philological monograph on Latin accent placement and syllable quantity (the source Hayes 1995 builds on); our deciding quote is a 1903 school grammar. Would settle the muta-cum-liquida weight clause and the enclitic/secondary-stress questions behind the record's 'srule: none described' and the 13 exception-class mismatches.
